topics.topic: The duplicate-preserving input representation supplied to canonical_bytes
questions: Does this operation receive raw JSON text, a duplicate-preserving parsed representation, or an already parsed value that cannot detect duplicate keys?
Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text/bytes that still preserve duplicate members, or an already parsed value from which duplicate keys may have been lost?
What representation reaches `canonical_bytes` that still exposes duplicate object keys, and how is a duplicate detected after normal JSON decoding would have discarded it?

quotes:
Encode one value as RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes, or refuse a value JCS cannot
represent.
judgement.why: The quoted canonicalization contract was unchanged, and the change did not alter or newly depend on its input representation.

topics.topic: How authored file-fixture bytes are supplied to add_trial_case
questions: How do the bytes of authored input and expected-output file fixtures reach `functions.add_trial_case` so they can be persisted?
How do authored file-fixture bytes enter `add_trial_case`, which must persist them and later execute the trial with them?

quotes:
Value
   bytes and file fixtures go to the content-addressed area through
   `capability:store.put_value_bytes`, which stores equal bytes once (A18 rule
   4); `module:functions` writes their StoredValues — an input with the class its
   contract input port declares, an expected output with the highest class of
   the case's inputs (M21, A07 rule 3) — and the TrialCase in one
   `capability:store.record_change`.
judgement.why: The authored-fixture ingress issue already existed in this unchanged passage, and the change did not create its need to receive fixture bytes.

topics.topic: Store bootstrapping when storage is absent and handling of unknown schema versions
questions: What happens on first start when the data directory, SQLite database, content area or spool layout does not yet exist, or when an existing database has an unknown schema version?
What happens when the configured data directory, SQLite database, or required store subdirectories do not yet exist?

quotes:
Take the exclusive lock, check the data directory and remove temporary files
before any record is read.
judgement.why: The store-opening contract was unchanged, and the change did not newly make first-start creation or schema-version handling relevant.

topics.topic: Whether run read operations return all M19 inspection facts
questions: Must `get_run`, run listings and other operations returning a run include the omitted M19 inspection facts, or is the State 5 run answer intentionally narrower?
Does a run answer also include M19's inputs, pinned implementations, resumptions and `cancelled_by`, which are otherwise omitted despite A07 explicitly governing disclosure of run inputs?

quotes:
A run's answer, wherever an operation returns one, holds: `run_id`, the flow
version, status, starter and times, outputs produced, waiting points with
 their reasons and, for `owner_approval`, the `approval_id` of the element's
`requested` approval — one always exists while it waits (A10 rule 2), once ended the
reason per missing output (A13 rule 7), and, once a `failed` run's spool is
released, `released_by` and `released_at` (M19) — every operation returning a
run, `release_run` among them, returns this one answer.
judgement.why: The enumerated run-answer contract was unchanged, and none of the changes altered which M19 inspection facts a run answer exposes.

topics.topic: Whether trial expected_outputs must cover every output port or may be partial
questions: When expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every contract output port, or may it specify only a subset to compare?
When `expected_outputs` is present, must it contain exactly every contract output port, or may it name only a subset?

quotes:
A case passes when the execution succeeded and, if the case states expected
   outputs, every output's digest equals the expected one — a file output is
   recorded in the TrialExecution by digest, size and media type, keeps no bytes,
   and is compared with the expected file fixture by digest; a `many` file output
   equals its expected list when both have the same length and the digests are
   equal position by position, so order and repetitions count; outputs that
   validate but differ are `output_mismatch`.
judgement.why: The expected-output comparison rule was unchanged, and the change did not affect whether an authored expectation may be partial.

topics.topic: Allowed api_base_url components and operation-path joining rules
questions: Are user information, query, fragment, percent-encoded separators, or an existing base path allowed in `api_base_url`, and exactly how are they joined with the operation path?

topics.topic: Bounds on manifest-derived strings throughout persisted and returned data
questions: What bounds apply when manifest-derived strings enter bindings, prepared requests, approval previews, failure reasons or answers?

topics.topic: Encoding and validation rules for multipart part names and media types
questions: How are quotes, backslashes, control characters and non-ASCII characters in port names encoded or refused, and what syntax is required of a port media type before it is placed in `Content-Type`?

topics.topic: Error classification for missing captured-trial dependencies
questions: How are a missing implementation, source execution, StoredValue or SpooledFile classified by add_captured_trial_case?

topics.topic: Exact sandbox failure_detail formatting and truncation rules
questions: What exact failure_detail is returned for syntax errors, load failures, abnormal exits, limit failures and exceptions, including formatting and truncation order?

topics.topic: How a binding retrieves a manifest file at a specific revision
questions: How does a binding operation obtain a file at manifest_revision from manifest_location?

topics.topic: How a flow constant's value_schema is supplied
questions: Where is each constant's independently declared `value_schema` supplied?

topics.topic: How an earlier implementation is determined for rollback eligibility
questions: What makes an implementation “earlier”: submission order, prior activation, position before the current implementation, or merely being a non-current admitted implementation?

topics.topic: How arbitrary HTTP error bodies are retained and represented in failure_detail
questions: For an arbitrary, possibly non-UTF-8 error-response body, which bytes are retained and how are they represented as failure_detail?

topics.topic: How callers select the content-identity or digest domain
questions: How does the caller specify which identity or digest domain is being computed, and therefore which facts and list-sorting rules apply?

topics.topic: How callers translate canonicalization failures across data surfaces
questions: How must a caller translate canonicalization failure for function output, service data, manifest content, and request data?

topics.topic: How get_repair_view represents a slot with no implementations
questions: How is the NodeExecution page produced for a newly created slot that has no implementations?

topics.topic: How masked failure_detail length is measured and whether it describes original or truncated content
questions: Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit, and is it the length of the stored truncated detail or of the original detail?

topics.topic: How runs obtains operation-node port declarations
questions: How does `runs` obtain operation-node port declarations for readiness, input validation and delivery?

topics.topic: Size limits and failure behavior for outbound requests and approval previews
questions: What maximum applies to a derived JSON or multipart service request and its persisted approval preview, and what result occurs when it is exceeded?

topics.topic: The observable effect of revoking standing approval for read or draft-write nodes
questions: What observable effect does revoking a grant for a `read` or `draft-write` node have?

topics.topic: The stable reason values and fields associated with refusal codes
questions: What exact, stable reason values and associated fields may accompany each refusal code?

topics.topic: The textual representation of integers in path placeholders
questions: What textual representation is used for an integer before percent-encoding it into a path placeholder?

topics.topic: Tie-breaking order for flow edges and constants during canonicalization
questions: How are edges with identical endpoint-order keys but different guards, and constants with the same target but different values, ordered for hashing and first-failure selection?

topics.topic: When the MCP listener is parsed and bound and how late failures interact with recovery
questions: When is `mcp_listen_address` parsed and bound, and what happens if parsing or binding fails after recovery has already committed changes?

topics.topic: Where configured service identities are validated in startup ordering
questions: Which operation validates configured service identities before any manifest path is constructed, and where does that check occur in the fixed startup error order?

topics.topic: Whether continuing after approval guarantees an HTTP send or only re-reaches the element
questions: Does a successful approval decision guarantee an HTTP send, or only cause the element to be reached again, possibly ending or waiting without a send?

topics.topic: Whether inspection reads return complete state records or only explicitly listed fields
questions: Do `get_contract_version`, `get_implementation`, `get_binding`, `get_flow_version`, and related reads return the complete State 1 records, including identity, provenance and timestamps, or only the fields individually listed in their operation outputs?

topics.topic: Whether issuing a contract version into an already-used slot is allowed
questions: Does issuing a contract version for an existing slot succeed, or is every already-used slot name refused?

topics.topic: Whether many-valued inputs may satisfy path placeholders at proposal time
questions: May a `many` input port satisfy a path placeholder at proposal time, even though its runtime value can never be the required scalar string or integer?

topics.topic: Whether published record-less spool files count toward the run spool limit
questions: Do published but record-less files count toward the run spool ceiling before they are replaced or the run spool is removed?

topics.topic: Whether resuming a run guarantees HTTP requests or only re-reaches unreachable elements
questions: Does resume guarantee another HTTP request for every unreachable element, or merely re-reach every such element in order?

topics.topic: Whether spool-limit failure after a successful service response is a contract violation or internal error
questions: When spooling a successful service file response exceeds a spool ceiling, must `reach_operation_element` return a normal `contract_violation` conclusion or an `internal_error`?

topics.topic: Whether token-list reads are retried after failure when the restored digest is unchanged
questions: After a failed re-read, does every request retry the read even if the restored file has the same digest as the last valid file?

topics.topic: Which addresses or hostnames qualify for the plain-HTTP loopback exception
questions: Does loopback mean only a literal IPv4/IPv6 loopback address, a hostname such as `localhost`, or any hostname whose current DNS result is loopback?

topics.topic: Which execution and attempt records determine an operation element's current conclusion
questions: When an element has several NodeExecutions and EffectAttempts after one or more not_applied resolutions and resends, which records determine its current conclusion?

topics.topic: Which facts constitute a SpooledFile's identity
questions: Is a SpooledFile's identity all M22 meaning facts or only (run, producer node, map index, attempt, port, list index)?
